hints.title: Full Sorting Overhead
hints.text: Sorting the entire array takes superlinear time. If you only need the kth largest value, how can you maintain only the k largest candidates seen so far as you stream through elements?

hints.title: Top K Smallest Boundary Invariant
hints.text: If a collection maintains the k largest numbers observed, its smallest member is always the kth largest element overall.

hints.title: Bounded Collection Maintenance Procedure
hints.text: Use a min-oriented priority structure of fixed capacity k. For each number in the array, insert it. If the size exceeds k, remove the smallest element. After processing all numbers, the top of the collection is the kth largest value.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Maintains a min-heap of size at most k+1 across all N elements.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full sorting takes O(N log N) time and O(N) space. For large arrays with small k, sorting the whole array does redundant work.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining a structure of size k achieves O(N log k) time and O(k) auxiliary space, which outperforms full sort when k << N.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explanation of why a min-oriented collection of size k yields the kth largest element at its top, comparison with Quickselect O(N) average time, and handling duplicate numbers.

solutions.approach: Min-Heap of Size K with Streaming Eviction
